If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% in late horizon (day 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment includes recent negative spikes (≤-0.33) within last 3 days, add 3–5% downward bias to mid-horizon (day 15–24) to counteract bearish momentum.  
When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows steep upward trend, cap late-period growth at 1% above recent 7-day average to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is uniformly positive but forecast is flat or slightly declining, shift early-period (day 1–10) forecast 1–2% downward to align with sentiment-driven volatility.  
If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (≥2 negative entries in last 5 days), reduce forecast by 5–7% in early horizon (day 1–10) to reflect risk aversion.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, apply 1–3% downward correction in mid-horizon (day 11–20) to dampen sentiment-driven overconfidence.
